family_history: No family history of Parkinson's disease

social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife in ground-floor apartment
social_history.tobacco: Former smoker, 25 pack-years, quit 25 years ago

patient.chief_complaint: Three-year decline in walking, bladder control, and memory — family requesting admission for evaluation
patient.history_present_illness: An 80-year-old retired bank manager with CAD (CABG 12 years ago), hypertension, and hyperlipidemia was admitted for evaluation of progressive gait dysfunction, urinary incontinence, and cognitive decline over the past three years. His wife reports that his walking gradually became slower and more shuffling approximately three years ago. He initially dismissed this as 'getting old.' Over the past year his gait has worsened significantly — he has a wide-based shuffling walk and has had four falls, including one that caused a scalp laceration requiring sutures. He now uses a rollator walker full-time and cannot ambulate safely without it. He requires assistance to get dressed due to slow, clumsy movements. Urinary incontinence has been present for approximately two years — he has two to three episodes of soiling per week despite timed voiding strategies. His wife has noticed progressive cognitive deterioration: he cannot balance his checkbook, has become disoriented in familiar surroundings twice, and repeats the same stories in conversation. He has always been a sharp and precise man, and his cognitive decline is very distressing to his family. There is no tremor, rigidity, headache, or diplopia. His primary care physician obtained an outpatient MRI three months ago that showed significant ventriculomegaly and referred him to neurology. He is admitted for comprehensive NPH evaluation and tap trial.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented to person and place but not date (thinks it's 2023). MoCA 18/30. Severe deficit in delayed recall (0/5), executive dysfunction, poor clock drawing (no hands placed correctly), visuospatial impairment. No aphasia. Reduced insight into cognitive deficits.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Normal. No papilledema. PERRL. Vertical gaze full.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal tone, full strength. No resting tremor. No rigidity.
neurological_exam.sensory: Mild vibration loss at bilateral ankles. Light touch intact.
neurological_exam.gait: Severe gait apraxia. Wide-based, short-stepped magnetic shuffling. Cannot initiate without cueing. TUG 38 seconds (with rollator). 10-meter walk 32 seconds. Cannot tandem walk. Pull test — 4 or more steps backward, near fall.
neurological_exam.additional: Bilateral grasp reflexes present bilaterally. Snout reflex. No nuchal rigidity.

mri.impression: 1. Ventriculomegaly with Evans index 0.42. 2. Florid disproportionate sulcal effacement at high convexity with enlarged Sylvian fissures (DESH pattern). 3. Callosal angle 65 degrees on coronal imaging. 4. Severe corpus callosum thinning with upward bowing. 5. Diffuse periventricular FLAIR transependymal signal and very prominent aqueductal flow void. 6. Moderate periventricular and deep white matter signal change (Fazekas grade 2). Ventriculomegaly markedly disproportionate to cortical volume loss. Clinical correlation recommended.

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 15 cmH2O. WBC: 2 cells/mcL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 48 mg/dL. Glucose: 66 mg/dL (ratio 0.67). cytology: No malignant cells. beta_amyloid_42: 796 pg/mL (normal). total_tau: 212 pg/mL (normal). phospho_tau: 24 pg/mL (normal).

specialized_test.test_type: High-volume tap trial (45 mL) with quantitative gait analysis

findings.urinary: No incontinence episode at 24h; patient reports decreased urgency

specialized_test.impression: Positive tap trial. TUG improved 37% at 24 hours (38 sec to 24 sec); 10-meter walk improved 34% (32 sec to 21 sec); MoCA improved 3 points (18 to 21). Patient reported decreased urgency and no incontinence episode at 24 hours. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings: Normal LV size and function. EF 58%. No regional wall motion abnormalities.
Mild aortic sclerosis without stenosis. Mitral valve normal.
output.impression: Normal left ventricular systolic function. Ejection fraction 58%. No regional wall motion abnormality. Mild aortic sclerosis without stenosis. Mitral valve structurally normal. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. Clinical correlation recommended.
Negative — sparse-to-no amyloid neuritic plaque density. CL score 16, below the threshold of 24. Clinical correlation recommended.

Markedly hyperdynamic aqueductal flow. Peak velocity 28 cm/s (reference <18 cm/s); stroke volume 102 mcL/cycle (reference <42 mcL/cycle). Both values substantially exceed published normative ranges. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.proposed: VP shunt surgery in patient on aspirin 81 mg for CAD secondary prevention
warnings: Hold aspirin 5-7 days pre-operatively per neurosurgery standard
Risk of withholding: bare metal stent (>1 year) — acceptable to hold; CABG patient without stents — acceptable to hold aspirin 5 days
Resume aspirin 24-48 hours post-operatively once hemostasis confirmed — critical for CAD secondary prevention

findings.finding: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity — involuntary contractions at 110 mL. Markedly reduced cystometric capacity 175 mL.

output.impression: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity with markedly reduced bladder capacity. Involuntary contractions at 110 mL; maximum cystometric capacity 175 mL. Pattern is consistent with detrusor overactivity of neurogenic origin. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.query: severe iNPH florid MRI findings Evans index VP shunt outcomes age 80

results.title: VP shunt outcomes in elderly iNPH patients — age 75+ registry
results.key_finding: Shunt outcomes at age 75+ comparable to younger patients when tap trial is positive; Evans index >0.4 does not worsen outcomes; gait improves in 75% at 1 year

results.title: Cognitive recovery after VP shunting in severe iNPH
results.key_finding: Even patients with MoCA <20 at baseline recover 4-6 points on average post-shunting when amyloid PET negative

output.summary: VP shunt outcomes at age 75+ are comparable to younger patients when tap trial is clearly positive, based on registry data. Evans index >0.4 does not predict worse outcomes. Gait improvement following VP shunting typically occurs within weeks; cognitive improvement may take 3–6 months. Patients with MoCA <20 at baseline and negative amyloid PET recover an average of 4–6 MoCA points post-shunting in available series.

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Occasional premature atrial complexes, a benign finding. No acute ST-T changes.
ecg.interpretation: Largely normal ECG with a benign incidental finding

findings: No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

differential.key_features: Normal CSF biomarkers; negative amyloid PET (CL 16). Cognitive pattern is frontal-subcortical with severe executive dysfunction, not episodic-memory predominant.
Moderate white matter changes (Fazekas 2) from hypertension; however Evans 0.42 and strongly positive tap trial confirm NPH as dominant process.

differential.diagnosis: Normal pressure hydrocephalus complicating vascular disease
differential.key_features: Both processes present; NPH component is treatable and was the primary driver of rapid decline
No tremor, no rigidity, gait is wide-based magnetic not festinant

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Evans 0.42, callosal angle 65°, florid DESH, corpus callosum thinning

Cardiology clearance for elective neurosurgery (prior CABG)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: EF 58%, no significant valvular disease — low cardiac risk

critical_actions: Confirm normal opening pressure (15 cmH2O meets criterion)
Do not withhold VP shunt based on age alone — outcomes in 80-year-olds are comparable to younger patients
Cardiac clearance required given CABG history
Hold aspirin 5 days pre-operatively; resume 24-48h post-op
contraindicated_actions: Withholding VP shunt referral based on age (80 years) alone
Attributing entire cognitive syndrome to family history of Alzheimer's without ruling out NPH
Stopping metoprolol perioperatively — risk of acute withdrawal and cardiac event
key_reasoning_points: Most florid iNPH imaging in this case series (Evans 0.42, callosal angle 65°)
Three-year progressive Hakim's triad — prototypical iNPH with advanced disease
Strongly positive tap trial (37% TUG) despite severe baseline impairment — excellent shunt response
Negative amyloid PET despite severe cognitive impairment (MoCA 18) — all due to NPH
Advanced age is NOT a contraindication to VP shunting when tap trial is clearly positive
Prior CABG requires cardiac clearance and careful aspirin management perioperatively

red_herrings.data_point: Brother with Alzheimer's disease and severe cognitive impairment (MoCA 18)
red_herrings.intended_effect: Severe cognitive impairment with family history of Alzheimer's may lead to premature Alzheimer's diagnosis and failure to pursue NPH workup
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Normal CSF biomarkers and negative amyloid PET exclude Alzheimer's copathology. All cognitive impairment is attributable to iNPH with excellent recovery potential.

red_herrings.data_point: Age 80 with prior CABG — surgical risk concern
red_herrings.intended_effect: Clinician may be reluctant to refer elderly cardiac patient for neurosurgery
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Cardiac clearance (echo shows EF 58%, no active disease) confirms low surgical risk. VP shunt is a low-risk procedure with excellent benefit in strongly positive tap trial patients regardless of age.

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: Straightforward iNPH — most severe presentation (Evans 0.42, MoCA 18) in an 80-year-old with prior CABG. Florid imaging, strongly positive tap trial, negative amyloid PET. Age and cardiac history as surgical hesitancy red herrings.
